verification_notes.note: Merged with D3 to form K1 (revenue performance including segment breakdown and drivers) and contributes to K4 (profitability outcome). Adjusted to avoid overlap with D5 by focusing on headline revenue and high-level drivers, with segment details moved to K1.

Revised to form K2 (operational volume declines). Removed Botnica charter days detail (moved to K1 as revenue driver) to avoid internal combining of distinct operational metrics and ensure focus on volume declines.

Merged into K1 (revenue performance) to eliminate overlap with D1. Segment revenue changes and specific drivers (charter fees, electricity sales, ferry services, lease income) are now consolidated under K1 for a unified revenue narrative.
Kept as K3 (operating expense pressures). Factually correct and no overlap with other units; provides critical detail on major cost drivers.

Removed due to substantial overlap with D1 (overall Adjusted EBITDA decline) and K4 (profitability outcome). Segment Adjusted EBITDA details are incorporated at a high level in K4 without granular breakdown to avoid duplicate evaluation of the same performance metric.
Kept as K5 (investment activity). Factually correct, distinct from other units, and materially relevant for capital allocation context.
Kept as K6 (financial position). Factually correct and provides a standalone view of liquidity and capital structure changes.

Revised to form K7 (significant Q2 2026 events). Events are kept in a single unit as they are distinct Q2 occurrences without causal linkage, but each event is clearly itemized to satisfy distinct-event requirements. No overlap with other units.
Kept as K8 (market valuation). Factually correct and focuses on share price, capitalisation, and ownership—distinct from financial position and profitability units.

redundancy_check.note: All final units were cross-checked for duplicate evaluation targets. K1 covers revenue performance (including segment breakdown and drivers), K2 covers operational volumes, K3 covers expense pressures, K4 covers profitability outcomes, K5 covers investments, K6 covers financial position, K7 covers significant events, and K8 covers market valuation. No unit substantially evaluates the same content as another.

key_information_units.information: Revenue increased by EUR 1.4 million (2.4%) to EUR 59.3 million in H1 2026, with segment breakdowns of Passenger harbours (+2.9%), Cargo harbours (–2.5%), Ferry (+1.7%), and Other (+19.0%). Key drivers included higher charter fees from the icebreaker Botnica (EUR 0.9 million, +18.2%), increased electricity sales (EUR 0.6 million, +25.0%), and growth in ferry services revenue (EUR 0.3 million, +1.9%).
key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 6; KPI Table page 4; Segment Reporting tables pages 8-9

key_information_units.information: Operational volumes declined significantly: cargo handling fell 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes (mainly due to liquid bulk down 33.8%), passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million (with the Tallinn–Helsinki route down 2.6%), and vessel calls dropped 4.8%.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section pages 4-6; KPI Table page 4

key_information_units.information: Operating expenses rose EUR 3.9 million (24.0%) in H1 2026, primarily from fuel costs up EUR 1.4 million (47.6%) due to higher prices and severe ice conditions, electricity costs up EUR 0.7 million (28.8%), and technical maintenance/repair expenses up EUR 1.2 million (80.0%).

Operating profit decreased by EUR 4.7 million (25.7%) to EUR 13.6 million and profit for the period declined by EUR 4.3 million (41.7%) to EUR 6.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell EUR 4.0 million (13.5%) to EUR 25.8 million, mainly due to higher operating expenses, lower cargo/passenger volumes, and the absence of prior-year one-off gains (land sale profit and insurance indemnity).
key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 7-8; KPI Table page 4

key_information_units.information: Investments totalled EUR 3.5 million in H1 2026 (versus EUR 12.0 million in H1 2025), mainly for ferry engine replacement, upgrades to the quay at Paldiski South Harbour, and IT infrastructure. Q2 investments were EUR 2.3 million (versus EUR 8.4 million in Q2 2025).

As of 30 June 2026, total assets were EUR 615.0 million (down from EUR 622.1 million), loans and borrowings were EUR 173.4 million (stable), total liabilities were EUR 247.4 million (up from EUR 241.2 million), equity was EUR 367.7 million (down from EUR 380.9 million), and cash and cash equivalents were EUR 27.6 million (down from EUR 32.0 million).
key_information_units.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Financial Position page 18

key_information_units.information: Significant Q2 2026 events: (a) Tallinn City Council adopted detailed plans for Terminal A and D areas; (b) Icebreaker Botnica completed a 20-day North Sea project; (c) A EUR 32 million unsecured loan agreement was signed with OP Corporate Bank; (d) Up to 485 additional Regula ferry trips were ordered for summer 2026; (e) A EUR 19.2 million dividend was paid (85% of 2025 profit).
key_information_units.source_evidence: Significant Events section pages 15-17; Dividends section page 14

key_information_units.information: At 30 June 2026, market capitalisation was EUR 335.06 million (versus EUR 340.85 million at 31 December 2025). The share price closed at EUR 1.274 (versus EUR 1.296 at the start of 2026), with 22,559 shareholders (67.0% held by the Republic of Estonia).
